name: Crackhead Control
description: Crackhead Control is a high rubber-guard clinch that reinforces Mission Control by bringing the second leg high behind the opponent's head, helping retain posture control while the arms remain inside.
summary: Crackhead Control is a high rubber-guard clinch that reinforces Mission Control by bringing the second leg high behind the opponent's head, helping retain posture control while the arms remain inside.
overview:
The bottom player keeps the opponent close with a Mission Control leg and hand connection. The second leg rises high to reinforce the upper-body clinch behind the head. The opponent's arms remain inside and must still be managed before an arm-isolation attack. The bottom player adjusts from the hips while the top player works to recover posture and inside frames.

This is a facing guard configuration. Unlike the basic Invisible Collar path, it does not require first clearing an arm to the mat and clearing the neck; unlike Dead Orchard, it does not define a completed both-arm leg triangle. Terminology: Crackhead rubber-guard control.

Establish the first high leg and its hand support before adding the second leg. Reinforce the clinch without forcing the knees beyond a comfortable hip angle. Do not assume that high legs alone have isolated an arm or completed Dead Orchard.

The high clinch is optional: release if the knee is twisted, the neck is stacked, or either partner signals discomfort. Do not use high-leg closure as a neck crank.

Instructional sources: [Eddie Bravo — MTS 169: the Pump](https://www.10thplanetjj.com/techniques/mts-169-rubber-guard-the-pump/); [10th Planet Costa Mesa — basic path with double bagger](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W2OFKidf9lE).
key_principles: Start with broken posture: Establish the first high leg and its hand support before adding the second leg.
Bring the second leg high: Reinforce the clinch without forcing the knees beyond a comfortable hip angle.
Track both elbows: Do not assume that high legs alone have isolated an arm or completed Dead Orchard.
Keep knees close: Use hip position and connected leg pressure rather than pulling the feet against fixed knees.
Return to one-leg control: Lower the reinforcing leg while preserving the first shin connection if you need Mission Control again.
Open against a stack: Release and frame when the opponent compresses your upper back or you cannot comfortably maintain the clinch.

top.name: Crackhead Control Top
top.description: Crackhead Control top perspective: Avoid extending an arm between the high legs where it can be isolated. A second leg climbing behind your head increases the posture-control problem.
top.overview:
The top player is responsible for recognizing and defending the control. The bottom player keeps the opponent close with a Mission Control leg and hand connection. The second leg rises high to reinforce the upper-body clinch behind the head. The opponent's arms remain inside and must still be managed before an arm-isolation attack. The bottom player adjusts from the hips while the top player works to recover posture and inside frames.

Avoid extending an arm between the high legs where it can be isolated. A second leg climbing behind your head increases the posture-control problem. Build a balanced base and an early hip frame before the high clinch closes.

Undo the high-leg connection before attempting to stand tall or extract an arm. Do not answer the clinch by driving the partner onto the neck. Begin ordinary guard passing once the shoulders and arms are free of the high enclosure.

bottom.name: Crackhead Control Bottom
bottom.description: Crackhead Control bottom perspective: Establish the first high leg and its hand support before adding the second leg. Reinforce the clinch without forcing the knees beyond a comfortable hip angle.
bottom.overview:
The bottom player is responsible for maintaining the control. The bottom player keeps the opponent close with a Mission Control leg and hand connection. The second leg rises high to reinforce the upper-body clinch behind the head. The opponent's arms remain inside and must still be managed before an arm-isolation attack. The bottom player adjusts from the hips while the top player works to recover posture and inside frames.

Establish the first high leg and its hand support before adding the second leg. Reinforce the clinch without forcing the knees beyond a comfortable hip angle. Do not assume that high legs alone have isolated an arm or completed Dead Orchard.

Use hip position and connected leg pressure rather than pulling the feet against fixed knees. Lower the reinforcing leg while preserving the first shin connection if you need Mission Control again. Release and frame when the opponent compresses your upper back or you cannot comfortably maintain the clinch.

This is a facing guard configuration. Unlike the basic Invisible Collar path, it does not require first clearing an arm to the mat and clearing the neck; unlike Dead Orchard, it does not define a completed both-arm leg triangle. The high clinch is optional: release if the knee is twisted, the neck is stacked, or either partner signals discomfort. Do not use high-leg closure as a neck crank.

Two high legs do not make the torso immune to chest pressure. Preserve space with the available inside arm and the supported knees; open the clinch before the passer can fold your shoulders and hips into a neck stack.
